 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [1962, 1963, 1964, 1965, 1966, 1967, 1968, 1969, 1970, 1971, 1972],
    'United States': [215.0, 208.0, 200.0, 195.0, 190.0, 200.0, 205.0, 203.0, 195.0, 185.0, 180.0],
    'West Germany': [32.0, 33.5, 36.0, 34.0, 22.5, 25.0, 29.0, 31.0, 27.0, 24.0, 20.0],
    'Japan': [14.5, 16.2, 18.0, 20.1, 23.0, 28.0, 32.0, 30.0, 25.0, 20.0, 15.0],
    'France': [9.0, 9.5, 10.0, 9.2, 8.0, 8.8, 11.0, 10.5, 9.0, 8.0, 7.5],
    'United Kingdom': [6.0, 6.3, 7.0, 6.8, 5.0, 5.8, 8.5, 8.0, 7.2, 6.8, 6.5],
    'GDP Growth US': [6.1, 4.4, 5.8, 6.4, 6.5, 2.5, 4.8, 3.1, 0.2, 3.4, 5.3],

    'GDP Growth Japan': [7.1, 10.5, 13.1, 5.1, 10.5, 11.0, 12.3, 12.1, 10.2, 4.3, 18.7]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars=['Year'], value_vars=['United States', 'West Germany', 'Japan', 'France', 'United Kingdom'],
                    var_name='Country', value_name='Trade Balance (USD Billion)')
df_gdp = df.melt(id_vars=['Year'], value_vars=['GDP Growth US', 'GDP Growth Germany', 'GDP Growth Japan'],
                 var_name='GDP Country', value_name='GDP Growth (%)')

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

ax1 = plt.gca()
ax2 = ax1.twinx()

sns.lineplot(data=df_melted, x='Year', y='Trade Balance (USD Billion)', hue='Country',
             ax=ax1, palette='Set2', linewidth=2.5)
sns.lineplot(data=df_gdp, x='Year', y='GDP Growth (%)', hue='GDP Country',
             ax=ax2, palette='Dark2', linestyle='--', linewidth=2.5)

ax1.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
ax1.set_ylabel('Trade Balance (USD Billion)', fontsize=12)

ax1.set_title('Trade Balance and GDP Growth by Country (1962-1972)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.9), title='Trade Balance')

West Germany's GDP growth depicted by the dark orange dashed line also varies, starting at 3.4% in 1962, peaking at 7.5% in 1969, and showing a slight decline in subsequent years. The chart effectively highlights the relationship and trends between trade balance and economic growth for these countries over the specified period.

import ast
source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
tree = ast.parse(source)
data_node = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == "data" for t in n.targets))
original_data = ast.literal_eval(data_node.value)
corrections = {}
for country in original_data:
    if country == "Year":
        continue
    if country.startswith("GDP Growth"):
        rows = table[table["GDP Country"] == country]
        col = "GDP Growth (%)"
    else:
        rows = table[table["Country"] == country]
        col = "Trade Balance (USD Billion)"
    expected = rows.set_index("Year")[col].reindex(original_data["Year"]).tolist()
    for year, old, new in zip(original_data["Year"], original_data[country], expected):
        if old != new:
            print(f"Mismatch: {country}, {year}: {old} -> {new}")
            corrections[(country, year)] = new

# Change only the differing numeric entries in the data dictionary.
lines = source.splitlines()
for country, year in corrections:
    node = next(v for k, v in zip(data_node.value.keys, data_node.value.values)
                if ast.literal_eval(k) == country)
    value_node = node.elts[original_data["Year"].index(year)]
    line_index = value_node.lineno - 1
    lines[line_index] = (lines[line_index][:value_node.col_offset]
                         + repr(float(corrections[(country, year)]))
                         + lines[line_index][value_node.end_col_offset:])
source = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
source = source.replace(
    "ax2.legend(['GDP Growth Japan', 'GDP Growth Germany', 'GDP Growth US'],",
    "ax2.legend("
)
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
print("GDP legend:", [text.get_text() for text in ax2.get_legend().get_texts()])
print("Title:", ax1.get_title())
print("Axis limits:", ax1.get_ylim(), ax2.get_ylim())
for name, group in table.dropna(subset=["GDP Country"]).groupby("GDP Country", sort=False):
    line = ax2.lines[list(df_gdp["GDP Country"].unique()).index(name)]
    expected = group.sort_values("Year")["GDP Growth (%)"].to_numpy()
    import numpy as np
    assert np.allclose(line.get_ydata(), expected)
    print(name, "verified; color:", line.get_color())
